description.narrative:
The general objective of the contribution is to promote democratic, egalitarian, inclusive, and representative decision-making processes at the regional level. The specific objective is to strengthen gender parity in democracy at all levels of participation and decision-making in the public and political life of women in Latin America. These objectives will be achieved through three results:
Result 1: Feminist and women's organizations expand political rights in favor of women through democratic frameworks and public policies aimed at achieving substantive equality.
Result 2: Strengthened coordinated advocacy among feminist movements, alliances, diverse feminist and women's expressions, and other allied actors for the adoption of global standards that consolidate Gender Parity Democracy.
Result 3: A strengthened regional civic agenda for democracy based on the principles of justice, gender parity, and secularism.

The title of the contribution is: Parity Program for the Strengthening of the substantive participation of women, in their diversity, in Latin America and the Caribbean,
The Overall Objective is to promote democratic, egalitarian, inclusive and representative decision-making processes at the regional level.
The Specific Objective is to improve the application of substantive parity at all levels of participation and decision-making in the public, economic and political life of women in Latin America.
The programme has a regional perspective by addressing some of the challenges to achieving substantive democracies and parity that transcend national boundaries but are common to countries. In summary, it seeks to:
-Strengthen regional actors and solutions and capacity for cooperation in the region, in particular for gender equality and women's empowerment through targeted training for women from civil society organizations and women in decision-making positions (in legislative, executive, and judicial branches) to equip them with tools and knowledge to advance the definition and implementation of regional and national agendas on women's rights and the fight against violence.
-Strengthen the conditions for political participation, exercise of citizenship, transparency, and accountability through direct support to civil society networks and organizations to advance their agendas for the promotion, exercise, and defense of their rights (including Afro-descendant women, rural women and youth).
-Enhance capacities, cooperation and dialogue between civil society actors with national and regional institutions. Contribute to cultural change through the promotion of positive messages on gender equality, justice, democracy and the secular state.

Titeln på bidraget: Jämställdhetsprogram för att stärka kvinnors, i deras mångfald, reella deltagande i Latinamerika och Karibien. Det övergripande målet är att främja demokratiska, jämlika, inkluderande och representativa beslutsprocesser på regional nivå. Det specifika målet är att förbättra tillämpningen av faktisk jämställdhet på alla nivåer av deltagande och beslutsfattande i det offentliga, ekonomiska och politiska livet för kvinnor i Latinamerika. Programmet har ett regionalt perspektiv då det adresserar några av de existerande utmaningarna för att uppnå demokrati och jämlikhet som överskrider nationella gränser och som är gemensamma för olika länder. Sammanfattningsvis syftar programmet till att: -Stärka regionala aktörer samt utveckla lösningar och kapacitet för samarbete i regionen, med särskilt fokus på jämställdhet och kvinnors egenmakt. Detta ska uppnås genom riktad utbildning för kvinnor från civilsamhällesorganisationer och kvinnor i beslutsfattande positioner (inom lagstiftande, verkställande och dömande makten) för att ge dem verktyg och kunskap att främja och genomföra regionala och nationella agendor för kvinnors rättigheter och bekämpning av våld. -Stärka förutsättningarna för politiskt deltagande, utövande av medborgarskap, transparens och ansvarsskyldighet genom direkt stöd till civilsamhällets nätverk och organisationer för att främja deras agendor för främjande, utövande och försvar av deras rättigheter (inklusive kvinnor med afrikanskt ursprung, kvinnor på landsbygden och ungdomar). -Stärka kapacitet, samarbete och dialog mellan civilsamhällets aktörer och nationella och regionala institutioner. Bidra till kulturell förändring genom att främja positiva budskap om jämställdhet, rättvisa, demokrati och den sekulära staten.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Based on Diakonias 2025 reporting, the Program contributed to strengthening gender parity in democracy by supporting womens organizations, leaders and networks to expand their participation and influence in political and public life across Latin America. In a context marked by democratic backsliding, shrinking civic space and growing anti-gender narratives, reported results in terms of strengthened leadership, advocacy capacity and regional articulation among women and their organizations, contributing to more inclusive and representative democratic processes.
Under Result 1, the Program strengthened the capacity of feminist and womens organizations to promote and exercise womens political rights. During 2025, more than 3,800 participations -84% women- were reported in training, dialogue and organizational strengthening processes. According to Diakonia and its implementing partners women leaders, candidates, elected officials and rights defenders improved their ability to exercise political rights, identify barriers to participation and political violence, and engage in advocacy processes. Examples from Peru, Colombia, Paraguay, Bolivia and Guatemala indicate stronger understanding of the electoral systems, capacity to participate in politics, ability to exercise civic oversight on electoral processes, increased collective organization to advance common goals and engage more effectively in public affairs. The Program also maintained a focus on women facing intersecting barriers to participation, including Indigenous, Afro-descendant, rural and young women. Importantly, out of the total participations in training processes in 2024 and 2025, more than 2,700 corresponded to women in political leadership roles, candidacies or decision-making spaces.
Through Result 2, the Program supported womens organizations and allied actors to advance parity democracy and address political violence against women. Reported results suggest that participating organizations translated training and dialogue processes into advocacy actions, including policy proposals, public positioning, strategic litigation and engagement with institutional actors and regional mechanisms. In Mexico, implementing partners contributed to the defense of parity regulations before the Electoral Tribunal of Jalisco through a joint amicus curiae. In Peru, advocacy efforts helped sustain discussions on parity and violence against women in politics despite a restrictive political environment, while in Guatemala Indigenous and feminist organizations succeeded in placing gender parity, alternation and Indigenous womens political participation on the national public agenda. The Program also supported collective responses to violence against women in politics in Bolivia, Peru, and Guatemala and generated evidence on barriers to womens political participation in Honduras. At the regional level, partners contributed to discussions within the Follow-up Mechanism to the Belém do Pará Convention (MESECVI), and the XVI Regional Conference on Women, helping sustain regional standards on parity and political participation.
Under Result 3, the Program contributed to positioning a regional public agenda for democracy grounded in principles of justice, parity and secularism. Through the campaign Somos la mitad, Queremos paridad (We Are Half, We Want Parity), partners adapted a common regional narrative to diverse political, cultural and territorial contexts, helping position gender parity as a democratic issue rather than solely an electoral reform. The campaign was particularly relevant in countries with pre-electoral or electoral contexts like Bolivia, Honduras, Paraguay, Colombia, and Peru. Through the campaign the Program also strengthened the communication capacities of partner organizations through a shared regional identity for the Program, communication tools, digital diagnostics and technical support.
In parallel, collaboration with the polling initiative Barometer of the Americas 2025/26 generated evidence on public attitudes toward womens political participation in selected countries, providing valuable information to inform future advocacy and communication strategies. Participation in regional spaces such as the II Inter-Movement Meeting of Latin America and the Caribbean and the Creo y Defiendo (I believe, I defend) initiative further connected parity democracy with broader debates on democracy, human rights, secularism and resistance to anti-rights movements, strengthening alliances among feminist and democratic actors across the region.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
